newsitem.title: USA: Dole hopes White House meeting to help Mideast peace.
newsitem.headline: Dole hopes White House meeting to help Mideast peace.

text.p: Republican Presidential candidate Bob Dole said on Sunday he hoped the coming meeting on the Middle East by Israeli and Palestinian leaders would be a step toward ending the violence there.

He said in a statement from Bal Harbour, Florida, where he was campaigning, that "Neither the United States nor any other part can impose a solution. The role of the United States, should, as always, be that of friend and facilitator."

President Bill Clinton earlier on Sunday announced that Israeli President Benjamin Netanyahu and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat had accepted his invitation to meet in Washington to try to end the violence that erupted after Israel opened a tunnel near Jerusalem's al-Aqsa mosque.
Dole said "This violence is a painful reminder that too many differences have been glossed over in earlier stages of the peace process.

He said the fact that the leaders of Egypt and Jordan, invited along with Arafat, may be joining Netanyahu to discuss the problems face-to-face "could be, and we hope will be, a step toward ending the violence."
